summary: `iceberg_rs` — Apache Iceberg for Mojo, over a Rust cdylib wrapping iceberg-rust.
description:
Mirrors lancedb.mojo's FFI pattern: one relocatable library
(`ffi/src/*.rs` -> `$CONDA_PREFIX/lib/libicebergrsmojo.{dylib,so}`, built by the
`iceberg-shim` pixi package) loaded through an `OwnedDLHandle`. The handle is
passed as a BORROWED `read` param to every worker so Mojo's ASAP destruction
can't `dlclose` the library mid-call (the flare gotcha) — even though each struct
also owns a handle as a field, the borrow keeps it pinned across the C call.

Nothing but integers, raw buffers and UTF-8 bytes crosses FFI. Iceberg handles
(catalog, table, scan, batch) are opaque `Int` pointers; results that don't fit
in a register come back as heap C strings which `_take_string` copies out through
`ib_string_len` / `ib_string_copy` and frees — so no Mojo code ever dereferences
a foreign pointer.

    from iceberg_rs import Catalog

    var cat = Catalog.sql("sqlite:/tmp/cat.db?mode=rwc", "file:///tmp/warehouse")
    cat.create_namespace("sales")
    var t = cat.create_table("sales", "orders", SCHEMA_JSON, SPEC_JSON)

    var b = t.builder()
    b.int_col("id", [Int64(1), Int64(2)])
    b.str_col("region", ["eu", "us"])
    t.append(b.build())
    var snapshot = t.commit()

    var scan = t.scan(columns="id,region", filter='["=","region","eu"]')
    for batch in scan.batches():
        print(batch.int_col("id"))

structs.name: Batch
structs.summary: One Arrow record batch owned by the Rust side.
structs.description:
Columns are copied out on demand and cast on the way: `int_col` reads any
integer, date, time, timestamp or boolean column as `Int64` (timestamps in
microseconds since the epoch, dates in days), `float_col` reads any numeric
column as `Float64`, `str_col` reads any column as UTF-8.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, var lib: OwnedDLHandle, ptr: Int)

overloads.summary: JSON array of `{"name", "type", "nullable"}` for the batch's columns.
Column `name` as `Int64`. Nulls read back as 0 — use `validity` to tell them apart.
Column `name` as `Float64`. Nulls read back as 0.0.
Column `name` as `Bool`. Nulls read back as False.
Column `name` as UTF-8 strings. Nulls read back as empty strings.
One flag per row of column `name`: True when the value is present.
Export this batch through the Arrow C Data Interface as a struct array (one child per column) — the shape marrow's `c_data.mojo` imports.

structs.name: ArrowCData
structs.summary: Storage for one Arrow C Data Interface struct pair.
structs.description:
The two structs live in `Int64`-backed Mojo buffers (guaranteed 8-byte
aligned, sized from the shim's own `sizeof`), so a consumer such as marrow can
read them straight from `array_ptr()` / `schema_ptr()`. Releasing is automatic:
the destructor calls the structs' `release` callbacks through `ib_arrow_release`.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, var lib: OwnedDLHandle, sizer: OwnedDLHandle)

overloads.summary: Address of the `ArrowArray` struct.
Address of the `ArrowSchema` struct.

structs.name: Scan
structs.summary: A planned table scan. Pull batches with `next()` until it returns an empty `Optional`, or inspect the plan with `plan_files()` without reading any data.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, var lib: OwnedDLHandle, ptr: Int)

overloads.summary: JSON array of the file scan tasks: data file path, format, record count, byte range, and any delete files that apply to each.
The next record batch, or `None` at the end of the stream.
The next record batch straight through the Arrow C Data Interface, skipping the opaque handle entirely.
Drain the scan into a list of batches. Convenient for the small results a parity check produces; stream with `next()` for large tables.

structs.name: BatchBuilder
structs.summary: Builds one record batch column by column against a table's schema.
structs.description:
Each `*_col` call names a column of the table; the values are cast to the
column's declared type on the Rust side, so `int_col` feeds `int`, `long`,
`date` (days) and `timestamp` (microseconds) columns alike. Columns you leave
out must be optional in the schema; they are filled with nulls.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, var lib: OwnedDLHandle, ptr: Int)
def int_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[Int64])
def int_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[Int64], valid: List[Bool])
def float_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[Float64])
def float_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[Float64], valid: List[Bool])
def bool_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[Bool])
def bool_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[Bool], valid: List[Bool])
def str_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[String])
def str_col(mut self, name: String, values: List[String], valid: List[Bool])

overloads.summary: Assemble the staged columns into a `Batch`.

structs.name: Table
structs.summary: A loaded Iceberg table: metadata, scans, and append/commit.
structs.description:
iceberg-rust 0.10 is append-only. `append` writes Parquet data files right
away and stages them; `commit` turns everything staged into exactly one new
snapshot and returns its id.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, var lib: OwnedDLHandle, ptr: Int)

overloads.summary: Re-load from the catalog, picking up snapshots committed elsewhere.
The table's full current `metadata.json` text.
The current schema in Iceberg metadata JSON form.
The default partition spec as JSON.
JSON array of the table's snapshots, oldest first.
The table's base location.
The current snapshot id, or 0 when the table has no snapshot yet.
A `BatchBuilder` bound to this table's schema.
Stage `batch` for append: writes its Parquet data file(s) now and remembers them until `commit`.

overloads.signature: def append_c_data(mut self, mut data: ArrowCData)
overloads.summary: Stage an Arrow C Data Interface struct pair for append. Consumes the pair — `data` is inert afterwards.
Data files staged but not yet committed.
Commit every staged append as one new snapshot; returns its id. With nothing staged this is a no-op returning the current snapshot id.
Drop every staged (uncommitted) append.
Scan every column of the current snapshot.
Scan a comma-separated column projection of the current snapshot.

overloads.signature: def scan(self, columns: String, filter: String) -> Scan
overloads.summary: Scan a projection of the current snapshot under a filter (see the filter DSL in the README).

overloads.signature: def scan(self, columns: String, snapshot_id: Int64, filter: String) -> Scan
overloads.summary: Scan `columns` (empty for all) of `snapshot_id` (0 for current) under `filter` (empty for none).

structs.name: Catalog
structs.summary: An Iceberg catalog: REST, or SQL over sqlite/postgres/mysql.

overloads.signature: def __init__(out self, var lib: OwnedDLHandle, ptr: Int)
def sql(uri: String, warehouse: String) -> Self
overloads.summary: A SQL catalog. `uri` is an sqlx connection string (`sqlite:/abs/path/catalog.db?mode=rwc`, `postgres://…`, `mysql://…`) and `warehouse` is the data root (`file:///…`, `s3://…`). The sqlite flavour needs no infrastructure at all — it is what the test-suite uses.
A REST catalog with no warehouse hint and no extra properties.

overloads.signature: def rest(uri: String, warehouse: String, props_json: String) -> Self
overloads.summary: A REST catalog. `props_json` is a JSON object of extra properties passed to the REST client — OAuth2 (`credential`, `oauth2-server-uri`, `scope`, `token`) and `header.*` entries go here. See `examples/rest_polaris.md`.
JSON array of top-level namespaces, each a dotted string.
JSON array of the namespaces under `parent` (empty for top level).

overloads.signature: def create_namespace(mut self, ns: String, props_json: String)

overloads.summary: JSON array of the table names in `ns`.

overloads.signature: def table_exists(self, ns: String, name: String) -> Bool
def load_table(self, ns: String, name: String) -> Table
def drop_table(mut self, ns: String, name: String)
def create_table(mut self, ns: String, name: String, schema_json: String) -> Table

overloads.signature: def create_table(mut self, ns: String, name: String, schema_json: String, partition_spec_json: String) -> Table
